claim_sentence: Each Mn(II) ion deposited in the SEI causes trapping of ~10^2 additional Li+ ions, hastening depletion of cyclable lithium.
notes: THE only literature number behind the catalytic amplification (Loop B, gap G7). Must determine: exact sentence, whether 10^2 is fitted or asserted, its uncertainty, and the composition of the Mn-free control (believed NCA, which changes Ni AND Co, not just Mn). If asserted rather than fitted, the manuscript must say 'estimated', not 'measured'. CC-BY: full text reachable.

claim_sentence: Parasitic current increases were observed for all preformed SEIs when Mn(II) was present.
search_any: parasitic current; parasitic currents; preformed SEI
notes: MOST IMPORTANT FETCH. Directly kills the old 'never measured' claim and is the paper we must not misrepresent. Need: size of the parasitic-current rise, whether reported per ppm Mn, quantitative SEI-chemistry dependence, concentration range. A scaling law here would narrowly CLOSE gap G7; its absence sharpens G7. Extract any ppm/current pair as a rate. NOTE: the needle is the distinctive phrase, NOT 'Mn2+' -- a paper with this title contains 'Mn' everywhere and would return a meaningless guaranteed hit.

claim_sentence: Dissolved transition metal causes loss of lithium inventory at the anode, with an S-shape evolution of capacity.
search_any: loss of lithium inventory; lithium inventory; S-shape; S shape
notes: Mechanistic anchor for Loop B AND the nominated P3 dataset. Need: actual LLI vs LAM numbers, whether temperature was the ONLY variable, whether any dose-dependent arm exists. Decides whether P3 is 'reanalysis of existing data' or 'needs new experiment' -- months of work vs days.

claim_sentence: Interphase-bound and metallic lithium cannot be separated by coulometry; measured inactive Li is partitioned between SEI species and dead Li0.
search_any: inactive lithium; LiH; lithium hydride; partition; dead lithium
notes: Cited for a METHOD claim: that interphase-bound and metallic Li cannot be separated by coulometry. Need the actual partition numbers on GRAPHITE so we do not overstate the impossibility. If they DO separate them, our method claim is wrong and the sentence must be rewritten. ChemRxiv preprint 403s here; fetch published.

claim_sentence: 'Snowball' denotes a degradation class in which capacity fade accelerates with continued cycling.
notes: SINGLE PAPER MOST LIKELY TO CONTAIN PRIOR ART AGAINST THE THESIS. Need their EXACT definition of 'snowball' and whether they attribute a MECHANISM or only a SHAPE. Our novelty claim depends on the answer: if they give a mechanistic account overlapping our feedback loops, the novelty sentence must be narrowed.

claim_sentence: Manganese dissolution from spinel proceeds at 1-10 ppm/cycle under mild conditions and tens to hundreds of ppm/cycle under aggressive conditions.
search_any: ppm/cycle; ppm cycle; ppm per cycle
notes: THE SINGLE WEAKEST NUMBER IN THE PROJECT and the highest-value fetch. The entire ~74x mole-for-mole shortfall argument (~40x if the two percentages are compared directly) runs on '5 ppm/cycle', and this review is the ONLY source for a ppm/cycle range. Verify both bounds AND the conditions separating 'mild' from 'aggressive'. If the honest rate is 50 ppm/cycle the shortfall falls to ~4x and the central quantitative claim weakens substantially. NOT YET CITED -- add to bibliography if used.

claim_sentence: Cracks do not propagate below a critical particle size of 2.5 um at rates below 5C.
notes: Supplies the critical particle size behind the stress/fracture margin ~1. Need the criterion's exact form (energy release rate? stress intensity?) and its RATE dependence, since our argument is rate-sensitive. If the 2.5 um figure is absent or conditional on a different rate, the margin-~1 argument must be re-derived.

claim_sentence: In situ observation shows single-crystal NMC811 fractures, but differently from polycrystalline secondary particles.
notes: Supplies prediction P5 (single-crystal vs polycrystalline differ in knee sharpness). ALSO A TARGET-JOURNAL CITATION: citing it well matters for fit with Batteries & Supercaps. Manual mode: the evidence is a qualitative observation, so a keyword hit proves only that the paper is on topic.

claim_sentence: Operando electrochemical impedance spectroscopy detects the onset of lithium plating during fast charging.
search_any: operando; plating onset; onset of lithium plating
notes: Supplies the claim that a plating-onset transition of this shape has been published. Need the SHAPE (what changes at onset) and the detection THRESHOLD (how small a plating fraction). The threshold is reused as the plating control in the P3 experiment spec, so a number here propagates into §5.

claim_sentence: Cryogenic electron microscopy finds nickel impurities within the solid-electrolyte interphase of lithium-metal anodes.
notes: Cited for TM entering the interphase. Need the measured Ni content (atomic % or ppm) and its effect. If Ni is present only as trace, the sentence 'TM enters the interphase' is fine but must not imply the quantity is large. Manual mode: qualitative claim.

claim_sentence: The solvent chemistry -- notably ethylene carbonate and tetramethylene sulfone -- governs the rate of transition-metal dissolution from the cathode.
context_any: ethylene carbonate; sulfolane; dissolution; transition metal
notes: Supplies the solvent-chemistry dependence of dissolution. Need rates in a COMPARABLE UNIT (ppm/cycle, ug/cm2/cycle, or fraction/cycle) so the claim carries a number rather than a direction. RSC: 403s in this environment.

context_any: crossover; cross talk; impedance; SEI; anode
notes: Loop B's causal arrow in one paper. Closed access, no preprint found -- if the PDF cannot be obtained, this citation must rest on the abstract and the manuscript must say so. Manual mode.
